title: Cached session resolution for a search API
name: Search session resolver

locateQuestion.prompt: Is there a defect in how this code decides whether a session is still valid? If so, mark the line(s) where it is; otherwise answer that there is none.
locateQuestion.explanation: The cache hit path only checks how long ago the entry was cached, not record.expiresAt. A session cached shortly before it expires keeps authenticating for up to five more minutes after its expiry. The store path checks expiresAt <= t, but the cache path skips it. The cache hit should also require cached.record.expiresAt > t.

choiceQuestions.prompt: The service runs as several instances behind a load balancer, each with its own SessionResolver. A user logs out through instance A. What happens to requests with the same session id that reach instance B?
choices: They are rejected immediately, because revoke deletes from the shared store
They are rejected, because logout clears the cookie on all instances
They fail with a 500 because B's cache and the store disagree
They may still be accepted for up to the cache TTL if B had the session cached
choiceQuestions.explanation: revoke() clears only A's in-memory Map and the store. B's resolve() returns from its own cache while t - cachedAt < CACHE_TTL_MS, without consulting the store. Nothing propagates revocation to other instances, logout does not touch cookies, and there is no consistency check that would cause a 500.

choiceQuestions.prompt: When the cache holds MAX_CACHED entries and a new session is remembered, which entry is evicted?
choices: The entry that was inserted earliest still present in the Map
The entry closest to its expiresAt
choiceQuestions.explanation: Map iterates keys in insertion order, so keys().next().value is the oldest insertion. Cache hits do not re-insert, so it is FIFO, not LRU; expiry and randomness play no role.

choiceQuestions.prompt: A user whose principal.indexes is ["products"] calls search with index "orders". What prevents them from reading another tenant's data if they had access to "orders"?
choices: Nothing; the index name alone determines which documents are returned
The backend query is always passed principal.tenantId, so results are scoped to the caller's tenant
The limit cap of 100 bounds how much data can leak
The session cookie encodes the tenant and the backend reads it
choiceQuestions.explanation: search() passes principal.tenantId, taken from the server-side session, into backend.query. Tenant scoping does not depend on the index name or the limit, and the cookie only carries the sid.
